1.explanation: 1) ComboBox.js: This is the core implementation. It needs a new readOnly prop in the interface, propTypes, and logic to pass readOnly to the <input> element, suppress the clear and toggle buttons, and apply the read-only CSS class. 2) ComboBox.stories.js: The Storybook stories must include a read-only variant and expose the readOnly prop in the Playground controls so designers and developers can preview and copy/paste the read-only usage. 3) ComboBox-test.js: Unit tests should be added to verify that when readOnly=true, the input has the readOnly attribute, the menu does not open on click or typing, and the clear/toggle icons are not rendered or interactive. These files together encapsulate the missing read-only behavior, styling, and testing for the ComboBox component.
1.bug_scenario: The Carbon ComboBox component does not yet support a read-only state. When we set readOnly={true}, the input remains editable, the clear (×) and dropdown (▾) icons still display and are interactive, and the menu can still open. According to the design mockups, a read-only combobox should look like a filled, non-editable field (no clear icon, no toggle icon, gray text), and pointer events should be disabled. The provided screenshots show the desired spacing, color, and typography for the read-only state.
